declared_assumptions: Integer arithmetic is exact in Python with arbitrary precision
The recurrence X_(n+1) = (1103515245 * X_n + 12345) mod 2^31 is correctly implemented
The die mapping die_n = 1 + (X_n mod 6) is correctly implemented
The standard deviation sqrt(10000 * (1/6) * (5/6)) ≈ 52.7046 is the correct measure for the fairness criterion
data.discriminating_purpose: Establish the exact six face counts for the specified LCG over 10000 draws, plus a calibration trace of the first ten (X_n, die_n) pairs, to determine whether the generator is fair or unfair by the problem's numerical criterion.
data.hypothesis: The LCG X_(n+1) = (1103515245 * X_n + 12345) mod 2^31, die_n = 1 + (X_n mod 6), seeded at X_0 = 42, is UNFAIR over 10000 draws: at least one face count falls outside two standard deviations of the uniform expectation 1666.7 ± 52.7. The LCG's state space (mod 2^31, coprime to 6) creates a systematic bias.
interpretation_conditions: All six counts must be non-negative integers summing to 10000
The calibration trace must match hand-computed values: X_1 = (1103515245*42+12345) mod 2^31, die_1 = 1 + (X_1 mod 6), and so on for the first ten terms
Fairness is determined by whether every count falls within [1666.7 - 52.7, 1666.7 + 52.7] = [1614, 1719]
The simulation must be deterministic: the same code and inputs produce the same counts every run
rival_predictions: All six face counts fall within [1614, 1719], making the generator fair by the stated criterion
The die_n values cycle through only a subset of {1..6} due to the additive structure modulo 6, causing extreme unfairness
The counts cluster around 1667 but with face-dependent systematic offsets due to LCG serial correlation, with some faces just outside the tolerance
